Rashi on Chullin 17a:10:1.english: When the Merciful One prohibited - [He prohibited] meat eaten out of desire in the wilderness:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:11:1.hebrew: שהכניסו ישראל - אליבא דר' עקיבא, מהו לאוכלן אחר כניסתן? מי אמרינן כי אסר רחמנא בשר נחירה לאחר ביאה, הני מילי לנחור אחרי כן לאכול, אבל הנחורות ובאות מן המדבר, הואיל ובשעת נחירתן היתר היתה, תו לא מתסרי, או דלמא לא שנא? ודרוש וקבל שכר, הוא שצריכין אנו לעמוד על האמת, ואע"פ שכבר עבר:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:11:1.english: That Israel brought in - According to Rabbi Akiva, what is the law regarding eating them after their entry? Do we say that when the Merciful One prohibited the flesh of a animal killed by nechira after the entry [into the Land], this applies only to killing it by nechira afterward in order to eat it, but [animals] that were killed by nechira and then came from the desert, since at the time of their nechira it was permitted, they are no longer prohibited? Or perhaps there is no difference? "Expound and receive reward" (Sanhedrin 71a) - this means that we must arrive at the truth, even if [the matter] has already passed.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:1.hebrew: ובתים מלאים כל טוב וגו' - סיפיה דקרא: "ואכלת ושבעת":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:1.english: "And houses full of all good things, etc." - The end of the verse: "And you shall eat and be satisfied."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:2.hebrew: כתלי דחזירי - חזירים יבשים, שקורין בקונ"ש:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:2.english: Sides of pork - Dried pigs, which in Old French are called *bacon*.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:1.hebrew: אלא לאחר מכאן - דהיינו בשבע שחלקו, דלא שרא להו רחמנא טומאה אלא בשעת שלל, כדכתיב (דברים כ) ואכלת את שלל אויביך וגו'. שבע שנים כבשו, ושבע שנים חלקו, כדאמרי' בפרק אין נערכין (ערכין דף יב:):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:1.english: Rather, after this - That is, in the seven [years] that they divided [the land], for the Merciful One permitted them [non-kosher food, i.e., that which is forbidden] only at the time of plunder, as it is written (Deuteronomy 20): "And you shall eat the plunder of your enemies," etc. They conquered for seven years and divided for seven years, as we say in the chapter "Ein Ne'erachin" (Arakhin 12b).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:2.hebrew: שלל של עובדי כוכבים - כדכתיב (דברים ו) "אשר לא מלאת", וכתיב נמי "את שלל אויביך":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:2.english: The spoils of idolaters - As it is written (Deuteronomy 6), "which you did not fill," and it is also written, "the spoils of your enemies."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:1.hebrew: שנית הכל שוחטין - ומוקמת לה בנשחטין, כדאמרן "הכל טעונים שחיטה, ואפי' עוף":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:1.english: The second [mishna]: "All may slaughter" - And it is established as referring to [animals] that are being slaughtered, as we said: "All require slaughter, even a bird."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:2.hebrew: ולעולם שוחטין - נמי מוקמת ליה כדאמרן, דאשמעינן דאע"פ שגלו לא חזרו להיתירן הראשון, ואין בשר נאכל אלא בשחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:2.english: And always, they slaughter - You also establish it [i.e., the mishna] as we said, that it teaches us that although they were exiled, they did not return to their original permitted status, and meat may be eaten only through slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:15:1.hebrew: וכי תימא בין בצור כו' - דלאו בנשחטין אתא לאורויי, אלא בשוחטין:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:15:1.english: And if you say, "whether with a flint, etc." - That [the mishna] did not come to teach about those that are slaughtered, but about those who slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - כולה בשוחטין והכל שוחטין תרתי דתני במתני':
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:1.english: Rather, Rava said - The entire [mishna] is about "those who slaughter" and "everyone slaughters"; these are two [distinct statements] that [the Tanna] taught in the mishna:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:2.hebrew: חדא לכותי וחדא למומר - כדאמרן בריש פירקין (חולין דף ג.):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:2.english: One to include a Samaritan, and one to include a mumar (a habitual violator) - As we said at the beginning of the chapter (Chullin 3a).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:3.hebrew: בין בלילה - כשאבוקה כנגדו, כדאוקימנא (לעיל חולין דף יג:):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:3.english: Whether at night - When a torch is opposite him, as we established (above, Chullin 13b).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:4.hebrew: בין בראש הגג - ולא חיישינן, דלימרו לצבא השמים עולה לשחוט:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:4.english: Whether on the top of the roof - And we are not concerned that people will say, "He is going up [to the roof] to slaughter for the host of heaven."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:5.hebrew: בין בראש הספינה - ואע"ג דתנן לקמן (חולין דף מא.) אין שוחטין לתוך ימים, בראש הספינה שרי, דמוכחא מילתא דלנקר ספינתו הוא צריך:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:5.english: Whether on the deck of a ship - Even though we learned later (Chullin 41a) [in a mishna]: "One may not slaughter into the sea," on the deck of a ship it is permitted, since it is obvious that he needs [the blood] in order to scour his ship.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:1.hebrew: פגם ושדר פגם ושדר - עשה בסכין פגימות הרבה שאינן דומות זו לזו, ושדר לא"י לידע איזו אסורה ואיזו כשרה. כן עשה פעמים ושלש:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:1.english: He nicked and sent; he nicked and sent - He made many nicks in the knife that were not similar to one another, and sent [it] to Eretz Yisrael to find out which [nick] is forbidden and which is valid. He did so two and three times.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:2.english: They sent to him - This is a sign for you regarding nicks.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:3.hebrew: כמגירה שנינו - שפגימותיה מכוונות לעומקן, ויש לפגם שני עוקצים: כשאתה מוליך צפרנך מסוף הסכין לראשה, צפרנך חוגרת בעוקץ של צד הראש, וכשאתה בודק מראשה לסופה, צפרנך חוגרת בעוקץ של סופה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:3.english: We learned it like a saw - [This means] that its notches are aligned with each other in depth, and each notch has two points. When you run your fingernail from the end of the knife toward its tip, your fingernail catches on the point on the side of the tip. And when you check from its tip toward its end, your fingernail catches on the point on its end side.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:1:1.english: And all the more so now - Since they were exiled [from the Land].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:1.hebrew: לאסור להם בשר נחירה - כדכתיב בההוא קרא דכי ירחק ממך המקום וגו', וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:1.english: To prohibit to them the flesh of *neḥira* [stabbing] - As it is written in that verse: "If the place ... is too far from you, etc.," "then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock, etc." (Deuteronomy 12:21).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:2.english: That at the beginning - In the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:3.hebrew: הותר להם בשר נחירה - מהאי קרא נפקא ליה, דכתיב "כי ירחק" "וזבחת", מכלל דעד השתא לא נצטוו על הזביחה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:3.english: Meat of nechira was permitted to them - He derives this from this verse, as it is written, "If [the place] is far... then you shall slaughter," which implies that until now they were not commanded about slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:3:1.english: And now that they were exiled - Rav Yosef is saying this [to him]:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:1.hebrew: בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל - וקרא "ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו" (ויקרא יז), בקדשים כתיב. והאי דכתיב (דברים יב) "בכל אות נפשך תאכל בשר", לאו לאורויי היתירא בבשר תאוה אתא, אלא כדדריש ליה רבי אלעזר בן עזריה בפרק כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין דף פד.): לימדה תורה דרך ארץ, שלא יאכל אדם בשר אלא לתיאבון. "וכי ירחק" "וזבחת" - בא להזהיר על השחיטה כשיכנסו לארץ. ואע"ג דקרא בפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו על ידי מומין משתעי, כדמוקמינן בבכורות (דף לב.), אפילו הכי גמרינן חולין מינייהו, כדאמרינן בפ"ב (לקמן חולין דף כח.): מקיש צבי ואיל לפסולי המוקדשי', מה פסולי המוקדשים בשחיטה, אף צבי ואיל בשחיטה, וצבי ואיל חולין נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:1.english: Meat of desire was not prohibited at all - But the verse states, "And has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" (Leviticus 17); this is written about sacrificial animals. And as for that which is written (Deuteronomy 12), "According to all the desire of your soul you may eat meat," it did not come to teach that meat of desire is permitted. Rather, it is as Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya expounds it in the chapter of Kisui HaDam (later, Chullin 84a): The Torah taught proper conduct, that a person should eat meat only out of appetite. "And if [the place] is far" - "you shall slaughter" - this came to warn about slaughter once they enter the Land. And although the verse speaks of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed on account of blemishes, as we establish in Bekhorot (32a), nevertheless we derive non-sacred animals from them, as we say in the second chapter (later, Chullin 28a): [The verse] compares the gazelle and the deer to disqualified consecrated animals: Just as disqualified consecrated animals require slaughter, so too the gazelle and the deer require slaughter, and the gazelle and the deer are non-sacred animals.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:2.hebrew: בשר נחירה לא אישתרי כלל - הילכך לא תלה הכתוב בביאת הארץ אלא היתר בשר תאוה, וזביחה דכתיב בהאי קרא לאו בביאת הארץ נתלית, אלא אורחא דקרא למכתב זביחה באכילת בשר. אי נמי, למאי דדרשינן בבכורות (ד' טו.) "וזבחת ואכלת", אין בפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו אלא היתר זביחה ואכילה, ולא גיזה ועבודה. אי נמי, לאסור שחיטת חולין בעזרה, כדדרשינן ליה בקדושין (דף נז:) "כי ירחק" "וזבחת", בריחוק מקום אתה זובח, ואי אתה זובח בקירוב מקום:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:2.english: Meat of nechira was not permitted at all - Therefore the verse did not make anything dependent on entering the Land except the permission of meat of desire; and as for slaughter, which is written in this verse, it is not dependent on entering the Land. Rather, it is the way of the verse to write slaughter together with eating meat. Alternatively, [it is] according to what we expound in Bekhorot (15a): "And you shall slaughter and eat" - in the case of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed, there is only the permission of slaughter and eating, but not shearing and work. Alternatively, [it comes] to forbid the slaughter of non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard, as we expound it in Kiddushin (57b): "If [the place] is far" "and you shall slaughter" - at a distant place you may slaughter, but you may not slaughter at a nearby place.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:5:1.hebrew: ושחט - אלמא, נצטוו על השחיטה באהל מועד שבמדבר:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:5:1.english: And he shall slaughter - Evidently, they were commanded concerning slaughter at the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:1.hebrew: ונתנבלה - כגון על ידי פגימת סכין, או שהייה, או דרסה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:1.english: And it became a neveila - For example, through a nick in the knife, or a delay [in the slaughter], or a pressing [of the knife].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:2.hebrew: והנוחר - מדעת. ולשון נחירה, שקורעה לאורכה מנחיריה ועד החזה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:2.english: And one who performs nechira - Knowingly. And the term "nechira" [means] that he tears it lengthwise, from its nostrils to the chest.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:3.hebrew: והמעקר - סימנין. ובחיה קאי, דטעונה כסוי, כגון צבי ואיל:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:3.english: And one who uproots - [This refers to uprooting] the simanin [the windpipe and the gullet]. And it refers to a wild animal [ḥayya], which requires covering [of its blood], such as a gazelle and a deer.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:4.hebrew: פטור מלכסות - דכתיב "אשר יאכל" "ושפך וכסה", בראוי לאכילה הכתוב מדבר. ואפילו מאן דמחייב כסוי בשוחט ונמצאת טרפה, הכא מודה דשחיטה מיהא בעינן, דגמר "שפיכה" "שפיכה" משחוטי חוץ, והתם שחיטה כתיב. בפרק כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין דף פה.):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:4.english: He is exempt from covering - For it is written, "which may be eaten" (Leviticus 17:13), "he shall pour out its blood and cover it" – the verse speaks of [an animal] that is fit for eating. And even the one who obligates covering for one who slaughters [an animal] and it is found to be a *treifa*, here he agrees that we do at least require slaughter, as he derives [the word] "pouring" from "pouring" from [the law of] those slaughtered outside [the Temple], and there slaughter is written. [This is discussed] in the chapter of "Covering the Blood" (later, Chullin 85a).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:5.hebrew: אלא לר' עקיבא - על כסוי הדם במדבר נצטוו, ונחירתן היתה שחיטתן, והנוחר בזמן הזה נמי נבעי כסוי:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:5.english: But according to Rabbi Akiva - They were commanded concerning the covering of the blood in the wilderness, and their *neḥira* (stabbing) was their slaughter. [Therefore,] one who performs *neḥira* nowadays as well, we should require covering [of the blood].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:9:1.hebrew: אך כאשר יאכל - עכשיו צבי ואיל בטומאה, "כן תאכלנו" - לבקר וצאן משתכנסו לארץ. שאע"פ שאני מטעינן שחיטה לחולין משתכנסו לארץ, כקדשים של עכשיו, אין צריכין ליאכל בטהרת הקודש, אלא כצבי ואיל של עכשיו, שהטמא והטהור אוכלין בקערה אחת. אלא לר' ישמעאל כו':
Rashi on Chullin 17a:9:1.english: "Only, as the gazelle and the deer are eaten" - Now, the gazelle and the deer are eaten in a state of impurity. "So shall you eat it" - [this refers to] cattle and flock, once you enter the land. For even though I burden you with [the requirement of] slaughter for non-sacred animals once you enter the land, like the sacrifices of now, they do not need to be eaten in the purity [required for] sacred food. Rather, [they are eaten] like the gazelle and the deer of now, which the impure and the pure eat from one bowl. But according to R. Yishmael, etc.:

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:13:1.hebrew: כי אישתרי שלל של עובדי כוכבים דידהו לא אישתרי - לא גרסינן או דלמא לא שנא, דהלשון היה משמע שהיה מסתפק אי אישתרי כתלי דחזירי דידהו אי לא, וזה אינו; דמתחלה לא נסתפק מכתלי דחזירי דידהו, או במה שנחרו כשבאו, אלא במה שנחרו במדבר בהיתר. והש"ס הקשה לו, דאפי' דבר טמא אשתרי להו, כלומר דאפילו לנחור בתחלה הם מותרים, כל שכן מה שנחרו קודם. ומשני, דלמא שלל של עובדי כוכבים אישתרי להו ולא דידהו, ולכך אסור לנחור; והשתא שפיר מיבעיא לן במה שנחרו בהיתר:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:13:1.english: When the spoil of the idolaters was permitted, their own was not permitted - We do not have the reading "or perhaps it makes no difference," for the wording would imply that he was in doubt whether the "walls of pigs" (kitlei de-ḥazirei) of their own were permitted or not, and this is not so; for initially he was not in doubt about the "walls of pigs" of their own, or about what they had stabbed (naḥru) when they came, but only about what they had stabbed in the wilderness, with permission. And the Talmud challenged him: even an impure thing was permitted to them, meaning that even to stab [an animal] in the first place they were permitted, all the more so [what they stabbed] earlier. And it answers: perhaps the spoil of the idolaters was permitted to them, but not their own [property], and therefore it is forbidden to stab; and now it is well that we are asking about what they stabbed with permission:

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:1:1.hebrew: וכל שכן השתא דארחיקו להו טובא - לספרים דגרסי באלו הן הלוקין (מכות דף יט.) לעולם לא קידשה לעתיד לבא, אם כן לר' ישמעאל הותרו הבמות. וקשה, דאם כן מאי קאמר הכא לר' ישמעאל דארחיקו להו טפי? אדרבה, אקריבו להו טפי, כיון דהותרו הבמות:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:1:1.english: And all the more so now that they were distanced from them greatly - According to the texts that read in [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 19a): "It was never sanctified for the future to come." If so, according to R. Yishmael the high places (bamot) were permitted. And it is difficult: for if so, what does [the Gemara] say here, according to R. Yishmael, that they were distanced from them even more? On the contrary, [the place of sacrifice] was brought closer to them even more, since the high places were permitted.

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:4:1.hebrew: רבי עקיבא סבר בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל - תימה, מנא ליה הא? דלמא מר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא, ולא פליגי. וי"ל, אי לרבי עקיבא מיתסר בשר תאוה, אם כן היכי הותרה להם בשר נחירה? דבקדשים מודה דבעיא שחיטה, כדמשמע בסמוך; ואי בצבי ואיל, הא בקרא דדרשינן מיניה היתר נחירה כתיב בקר וצאן, כדכתיב כי ירחק ממך, וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך, מכלל דמעיקרא לא בעו זביחה. ומיהו קשה, דהוה ליה לאוקומי קרא דהיתר נחירה בבעלי מומין דלא חזו להקרבה:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:4:1.english: Rabbi Akiva holds that meat of desire (basar ta'avah) was not forbidden at all - It is puzzling: from where does he know this? Perhaps one Sage said one thing and the other Sage said another, and they do not disagree! And one can answer: If, according to Rabbi Akiva, meat of desire was forbidden, then how was the meat of nechirah (stabbing) permitted to them? For with regard to sacrificial animals, he concedes that they require slaughter (shechitah), as is implied shortly below. And if [it was permitted] with regard to deer and ibex [which are not sacrificial animals] — but in the verse from which we derive the permission of nechirah, "cattle and flock" is written, as it is written, "When [the place] is too far from you" (Deuteronomy 12:21), "then you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock," which implies that originally they did not require slaughter (zeviḥah). But nevertheless, it is difficult, for [the Gemara] should have established the verse that permits nechirah as referring to blemished animals, which are not fit for sacrifice.
